title: Rapid test for COVID-19 and flu
what: A nurse runs a soft swab inside your nose. The test shows COVID and flu viruses in 15 to 20 minutes.
why: For fever, cough, runny nose, or sore throat, to quickly find the cause of your illness.
duration: the swab takes about a minute; results usually come in 15 to 20 minutes
tell_doctor: If you get nosebleeds often or had nose surgery
If you have long-term illnesses or are pregnant

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: For a few hours before, do not use nose drops or sprays, and do not rinse your nose.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually do not eat or drink for 30 to 60 minutes before. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The test works best in the first days of illness.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit and tilt your head back a little
The swab goes into your nostril and is turned for a few seconds
The swab is dipped in liquid, and drops go on a test strip
The result is read after 15 to 20 minutes
feel: It tickles. You may want to sneeze, and your eyes may water
after: If the test is negative but you are ill, it may be repeated, or a PCR test may be done
While ill, limit contact with others, wear a mask, and air out the room
red_flags: Trouble breathing, chest pain, or confusion: call emergency services
A fever over 39°C (102°F) that does not come down with medicine: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: How is a rapid test different from PCR?
faq.a: A rapid test is faster but less accurate. PCR catches the virus even in small amounts.

faq.q: Does a negative test mean it is not COVID?
faq.a: Not always. In the first hours of illness, there may be too little virus. Your doctor may order a repeat or a PCR test.

reminders.text: Rapid test soon. No nose drops, and do not eat for 30 to 60 minutes before the swab.
